major_risks.risk: Tariffs, trade restrictions and geopolitical tensions could disrupt the supply chain (a significant majority of manufacturing is outsourced to partners in China mainland, India, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam), raise costs, and reduce demand.
major_risks.source: Item 1A, Macroeconomic and Industry Risks (p. 6); Item 7, 'Tariffs and Other Measures' (p. 25)

major_risks.risk: The company faces supply constraints and rising costs for key components (advanced semiconductors, memory and storage) and for compute capacity, and expects these trends to intensify for memory and storage, which could hurt revenue and gross margin.
major_risks.source: Item 1A, Business Risks (p. 9); Item 1, 'Supply of Components and Computing Resources' (p. 3)

major_risks.risk: Legal and regulatory actions could force changes to its business or cost it fees, revenue or fines. They include the EU Digital Markets Act, the US App Store commission injunction (Epic Games), the DOJ antitrust suit, and the antitrust remedies affecting its Google search licensing revenue.
major_risks.source: Item 1A, Legal and Regulatory Compliance Risks (pp. 14-17); Item 3, Legal Proceedings (pp. 20-21)

not_in_report.question: The company's current share price today
not_in_report.answer: The report does not give a current share price. It does give historical reference points: the aggregate market value of shares held by non-affiliates (about $3,647,099,000,000 at March 27, 2026), average repurchase prices of $309.66–$329.22 per share in Q4 FY2026 (Item 5, p. 22), and a cumulative total-return index value (Item 5, p. 23). None of these is a price today.

not_in_report.question: The company's own earnings guidance for the next fiscal year
not_in_report.answer: The report contains no quantitative earnings or revenue guidance for fiscal 2027. It only says in general terms that gross margins will be subject to volatility and downward pressure and that memory and storage cost trends are expected to intensify.
not_in_report.source: Item 7, Gross Margin and Macroeconomic Conditions (pp. 24, 27)

not_in_report.question: An analyst's estimate of the company's fair value
not_in_report.answer: The report contains no fair-value estimate of the company. The fair values it does give relate only to financial instruments, such as the Notes at $64.0 billion (Note 10).

limits: The report says gross margin was helped by tariff refunds recognized in products cost of sales (Item 7, p. 27). It gives no amount for these refunds, so the analyst cannot isolate their effect on operating income.
Cash is only 36,305 as defined. Marketable securities of 100,630 are excluded, so net debt on the stated definition (43,806) is well above a net debt that nets all liquid investments.

Total financial debt uses balance-sheet carrying values and includes the hedge fair-value adjustment and unamortized discount in term debt. Principal outstanding is 78,678 for term debt (Note 10) plus 1,997 of commercial paper. Lease liabilities of 14,368 are excluded.

Capex is the line 'Payments for acquisition of property, plant and equipment' (9,041). The report notes data-center and AI infrastructure commitments, and other purchase obligations include the acquisition of capital assets, so future capex may differ.

The three risks were chosen by me from a long Item 1A, which does not rank risks by importance. Other risks the company lists, such as AI competition, cybersecurity and currency, are equally prominent.
The filing includes exhibits (stock plan forms, insider trading policy, and others) that contain no financial data and were not used.
